prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: insufficient (not scored)
  tan: 1.00
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
Summary of key commitments (ideological framing excluded)

- Tax, welfare and pensions:
  - Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises to income tax or VAT.
  - Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and create an age-related personal allowance so pensioners’ tax-free threshold at least matches the State Pension.
  - Child Benefit to be based on household income: tapered between £120,000–£160,000.
  - Tackle avoidance/evasion to raise £6bn a year.
  - Welfare reforms: tighten work capability assessments, overhaul fit notes via specialist assessors, tougher sanctions at 12 months, expand UC rollout, new Fraud Bill.

- Families, childcare, education and skills:
  - 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school (by Sept 2025); nationwide wraparound care by Sept 2026; Family Hubs in every local authority.
  - Ban mobile phones during the school day; attendance measures; register for children not in school.
  - Advanced British Standard replaces A levels/T Levels; English and maths to 18; expand teacher recruitment/retention premiums.
  - 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by restricting poor‑outcome degrees; Lifelong Learning Entitlement.
  - Mandatory National Service at 18: either 12‑month paid military/cyber placements (competitive) or 25 days civic service.

- Health and social care:
  - NHS funding to rise above inflation annually; +92,000 nurses and +28,000 doctors vs 2023.
  - Pharmacy First expansion; 250 new/modernised GP surgeries; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
  - Dental plan: 2.5m extra NHS appointments; contract reform; service requirements for newly qualified dentists; targeted “golden hellos”.
  - £3.4bn tech plan: NHS App as single front door; AI diagnostics; replace legacy IT; productivity reforms and 5,500 fewer managers.
  - Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health actions; implement Cass Review; single‑sex accommodation rights.

- Policing, justice and protests:
  - 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; facial recognition, knife seizure powers.
  - Harsher sentences for serious offences; four new prisons to reach 20,000 new places; expand tagging/community payback.
  - Martyn’s Law; anti-fraud measures; tighter protest controls (face coverings/pyrotechnics bans in scope).

- Immigration and borders:
  - Legal, binding annual cap on migration (work/family routes), falling each year; higher salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks and higher IHS/insurance where needed.
  - Illegal migration: monthly Rwanda flights, bring Illegal Migration Act into force, process claims in 6 months, end hotel use; more returns deals; pursue treaty reforms.

- Defence and foreign:
  - Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; at least 5% of defence budget for R&D plus 2% for exploitation; long‑term support to Ukraine.
  - Veterans Bill; NI waivers for dependants; improved recognition of service in benefits.

- Economy, business, infrastructure and trade:
  - Meet fiscal rules; no rise in corporation tax; maintain full expensing and consider extension to leasing; SME 10‑point plan (rates, VAT threshold review, finance access, prompt payment, regulation).
  - Digital: nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; automated vehicles law.
  - Transport: £36bn HS2 savings redeployed to regional schemes; £8.3bn potholes; Rail Reform Bill creating Great British Railways; nationwide PAYG contactless; £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.
  - Trade: complete India and GCC FTAs; implement CPTPP; maintain standards and exclude NHS from deals.

- Energy and net zero:
  - Annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets; new nuclear at Wylfa; grid and connections reforms.
  - Household energy‑efficiency vouchers; maintain price cap; standing charge review; Pumpwatch; keep levies lower than 2023; no road pricing or frequent flyer levy.

- Housing and planning:
  - 1.6m homes; scrap nutrient neutrality via one‑off mitigation fee; fast‑track brownfield in 20 cities; higher London densities; development corporations; protect Green Belt.
  - Permanent FTB SDLT threshold at £425k; new Help to Buy (up to 20% equity loan, 5% deposit); Mortgage Guarantee continues.
  - Renters Reform (abolish s21 after court changes); leasehold reform (cap ground rents; end forfeiture; enable commonhold); 2‑year CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; controls on holiday lets.

- Rural, farming, fishing, environment:
  - Farming budget +£1bn over Parliament (UK‑wide, inflation‑linked); legal food security target and UK Food Security Index; fast‑track farm infrastructure; 5‑year tapered seasonal visa scheme; £20m Farming Innovation Fund.
  - Replicate £100m UK Seafood Fund; seek more inshore opportunities in 2026 talks.
  - Environment: expand Blue Belt; moratorium on deep sea mining; tougher water sector penalties/bonus bans; river recovery network; tree/peat funding; forest‑risk commodities law; new National Park; stronger waste crime penalties; limit new incinerators.

- Communities, culture and drivers:
  - £20m endowments for 105 towns (plus more); extend Community Ownership Fund and UKSPF; more Freeports/Investment Zones.
  - Backing Drivers Bill: ban road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local votes on LTNs/20mph.
  - Maintain grassroots sport investment; Independent Football Regulator; creative tax incentives; BBC funding review and new complaints process.

- Sex and gender law:
  - Clarify Equality Act: “sex” means biological; one legal sex in UK law; statutory school guidance on gender‑questioning pupils with parental involvement.

- Union and devolution:
  - Protect internal market; extend UKSPF/towns/community funds to devolved nations; targeted transport/energy projects in Scotland, Wales, NI; implement Windsor Framework and legacy arrangements in NI.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key policies in the Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 (ideological framing removed)

- Economy and tax: Industrial strategy focused on green growth and skills; repair UK–EU trade links; responsible fiscal rules to reduce debt share; priority future tax cut via higher personal allowance; new/changed taxes including reversing bank tax cuts, Digital Services Tax at 6%, fairer capital gains, 4% levy on FTSE-100 buybacks, and a proper one-off windfall tax on oil and gas; expand British Business Bank; national financial inclusion strategy.

- Business, jobs and work: Abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; R&D to 3% of GDP by 2030; AI regulation promoting innovation and accountability; stronger late-payment enforcement; skills and training levy replacing apprenticeship levy; apprentices paid at least the minimum wage; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim £10,000); new “dependent contractor” status with basic rights; stronger sick pay; Worker Protection Enforcement Authority.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; 10-year home energy upgrade (free insulation/heat pumps for low-income households), social energy tariff, zero‑carbon standard for new buildings, decouple power prices from gas; no fracking or new coal; expand storage and interconnectors; support community energy; carbon border adjustment; associate UK ETS with EU ETS.

- Health: Right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours if urgent), 8,000 more GPs, expanded pharmacist roles and 24/7 booking; urgent NHS dentistry access and contract reform; mental health hubs for young people, routine mental health check-ups, a professional in every school; cancer treatment to start within 62 days; 10‑year estates plan; ambulance delay reductions; digital upgrades; drug policy shift including regulated cannabis market.

- Social care and carers: Free personal care; workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers, and a Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); cross‑party funding commission; paid carer’s leave and guaranteed respite; National Care Agency and portable care packages; kinship care support.

- Education and families: Per‑pupil funding to rise in real terms; repair school estates; tutoring guarantee; early years boost (extra free hours and tripled premium for disadvantaged children); maintenance grants restored; teacher workforce strategy and funded CPD; SEND reforms and funding; return to Erasmus+; parental leave/pay as day‑one rights, doubled statutory pay, extra month for partners; extend free school meals to all children in poverty.

- Welfare and pensions: Scrap benefit cap and two-child limit; cut Universal Credit wait to 5 days; replace sanctions with incentive-based support; protect triple lock; fair compensation for 1950s-born women; raise and widen Carer’s Allowance; disability benefit and assessment reforms; Independent Living Taskforce.

- Crime and justice: Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance/investigation for all burglaries; clear court backlogs; improve rehabilitation; domestic abuse specialists; Online Crime Agency; replace PCCs with local Police Boards; youth diversion nationwide; stronger fraud reimbursement; modern slavery protections; prison officer recruitment and resettlement plan.

- Nature and water: Turn water companies into public benefit companies; ban bonuses until leaks/discharges end; new tougher regulator, sewage tax, real-time discharge data; binding nature targets (including tree planting 60m/year), expand protected areas; Clean Air Act and new agency; deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics within three years; peatland and marine restoration.

- Food and farming: National Food Strategy; accelerate and fund ELMS (+£1bn/year); veterinary/plant health agreements with EU; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; support local abattoirs and sustainable procurement; fisheries sustainability; animal welfare bill, ban caged hens; bTB vaccines; fund alternative proteins.

- Housing and homelessness: 380,000 homes/year including 150,000 social; 10 new garden cities; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; ban no‑fault evictions, 3‑year default tenancies, national landlord register; councils able to end Right to Buy; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders; Rent to Own; plan to end rough sleeping and repeal Vagrancy Act; stronger controls on second homes/short lets.

- Local government and connectivity: Multi‑year settlements; more local powers including on second homes; gigabit broadband nationwide; rural support (post office hubs, fuel duty relief); bus franchising powers.

- Transport: Rapid EV charging rollout, restore plug‑in grant, cut VAT on public charging to 5%, 2030 zero‑emission new car/van sales; freeze rail fares, simplify ticketing; major rail electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail, review HS2 north; £2 bus fare cap and expansion; integrated ticketing; active travel networks; shift freight to rail; curb frequent-flyer emissions, tax private jets, ban short domestic flights with <2.5h rail alternative; airport expansion moratorium.

- Culture, media and sport: Protect public service broadcasters; Creative Europe participation; simple EU touring for artists; creative enterprise zones; tourism minister; anti‑SLAPP law; gambling levy, ad restrictions, affordability checks; independent football regulator.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work/student visa policy out of Home Office; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme; safe/legal routes including humanitarian permits; 3‑month service standard for asylum decisions; lift work ban after 3 months; flexible work visas replacing salary threshold; exemptions for NHS/care workers; expand Youth Mobility; reverse higher family visa thresholds; Windrush redress; repeal Right to Rent; limit detention and ban child detention.

- Rights and democratic reform: Retain Human Rights Act and ECHR; ban conversion practices; digital bill of rights; regulate biometrics; implement Istanbul Convention; votes at 16; proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; cap political donations; Lords reform; written federal constitution; ministerial code in law; stronger transparency and lobbying rules; citizens’ assemblies.

- Defence and international: Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; parliamentary vote on military action; arms export presumption of denial to human‑rights abusers; procurement reform; better housing/mental health for forces; rebuild EU cooperation via phased roadmap (agencies, MRAs, SPS, Single Market long‑term goal); restore 0.7% aid; support Ukraine (including seizing Russian assets); advocate ceasefire and two‑state process, recognise Palestine; address China/Hong Kong/Uyghurs; fund BBC World Service.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "A" | "B"
}
